statement: The report cites $68 billion of U.S. data-center projects blocked or delayed in the June quarter because of local opposition and resource constraints.
why: Siting and resource friction is a physical ceiling on how fast purchased accelerators can be energized, so it constrains deliverable capacity independently of chip supply.

impact.mechanism: Blocked or delayed shells and interconnects push out the point at which accelerators can be installed and drawn down, slowing effective capacity growth.

evidence.excerpt: the report cites '$68 billion' worth of blocked or delayed projects in the US in the June quarter due to local opposition and resource constraints

confidence.basis: Single secondary outlet citing a consultancy report; no primary filing or regulatory docket behind the figure.

entity: multi (data-center / AI infrastructure industry); Bain & Co (forecaster)
